cards.title: Interior Angle Formula
cards.problemText: Which formula gives the sum of interior angles of a polygon with n sides?
cards.solution: The sum of the interior angles of an n-sided polygon is given by S = (n - 2) × 180°.

cards.title: Supplementary Angle Quest
cards.problemText:
In the figure below, ∠ABD and  ∠CBD are supplementary angles. If m∠ABD=75, what is m∠CBD?
[IMAGE: ∠ABD = 75° forming a straight line with ∠CBD]
cards.solution: Supplementary angles add up to 180°. Therefore, m∠CBD = 180° - 75° = 105°.

cards.title: Simple Interest Formula
cards.problemText: Maria invested ₱10,000 in a savings account that earns simple interest at a rate of 5% per year for 2 years. Which formula should Maria use to calculate the simple interest I?
cards.solution: Simple interest is calculated using I = Prt, where P is principal, r is the annual rate, and t is time in years.

cards.title: Identifying Rational Numbers
cards.problemText: Which of the following is a rational number?
cards.solution: 0.121212… is a repeating decimal equal to 4/33, which is rational because it is a quotient of two integers.

cards.title: Regular Polygon Naming
cards.problemText: A polygon with six equal sides and six equal interior angles is a regular pentagon.
cards.solution: A 6-sided polygon with all equal sides and angles is a regular hexagon.

cards.title: Complementary Angles Sum
cards.problemText: The sum of two complementary angles.
cards.solution: Two angles are complementary if the sum of their measures is 90°.

cards.title: Definition of Discount
cards.problemText: Is the statement true or false: Discount is the amount deducted from the original price.
cards.solution: Discount is the amount deducted from the original or marked price.

cards.title: Definition of Unit Rate
cards.problemText: Is the statement true or false: A unit rate is a rate that has 1 as its denominator.
cards.solution: A unit rate is a comparison to 1 unit of another measure.

cards.title: Rational Number Condition
cards.problemText: Replace the underlined statement with correct mathematical statement: A rational number is a number that can be written as fraction ab, where a and b are integers and b=0.
cards.solution: Because division by zero is undefined, the denominator b must be nonzero (b ≠ 0).

cards.title: Number Line Direction
cards.problemText: On a number line, negative rational numbers are location to the _________ of zero. (direction)
cards.solution: Negative numbers are always positioned to the left of zero on a standard horizontal number line.

cards.title: Nature of Zero
cards.problemText: Is the statement true: Zero is neither positive nor negative.
cards.solution: Zero is the neutral point between positive and negative numbers on the real number line.

cards.title: Properties of Vertical Angles
cards.problemText: Which of the following statements DOES NOT correctly describe vertical angles?

answers.text: They formed from two intersecting lines.

cards.solution: Vertical angles are opposite angles formed by intersecting lines and are congruent, not necessarily complementary (summing to 90°).

cards.title: Recognizing Unit Rates
cards.expectedAnswer: Running at a speed of 24 kilometers per hour.
acceptableAnswers: Running at a speed of 24 kilometers per hour.
cards.problemText: Which of the following is expressed as a unit rate?

answers.text: Running at a speed of 24 kilometers per hour.

cards.solution: 24 kilometers per 1 hour has a denominator of 1 unit of time, which defines a unit rate.

cards.title: Fraction to Decimal Conversion
cards.problemText: Manuel is making a recipe that requires 38 cup of sugar. To better measure the sugar with a digital scale, he wants to convert the fraction to decimal. What is the decimal equivalent of 38?
cards.solution: Dividing 3 by 8: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375.

cards.title: Percentage to Fraction
cards.problemText: What fraction represents 50%?

cards.title: Earth's Water Percentage
cards.problemText: The ocean holds 97% of the Earth’s water. What is 97% in decimal?

cards.title: Decimal to Fraction Simplification
cards.problemText: What is the equivalent fraction of 1.25 in simplest form?

cards.title: Simplest Form Definition
cards.expectedAnswer: The GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1.
acceptableAnswers: The GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1.
cards.problemText: What does it mean when a fraction is in simplest form?

answers.text: The numerator is always smaller than the denominator.
The GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1.

cards.solution: A fraction is simplified when the Greatest Common Factor of its numerator and denominator is 1.

cards.title: Comparing Unit Fractions
cards.problemText: Which of the following fractions is the smallest?
cards.solution: When numerators are equal to 1, larger denominators produce smaller fractions: 1/6 < 1/5 < 1/3 < 1/2.

cards.title: Fraction on Number Line
cards.problemText: On a standard number line, where is -34 located relative to -1 and 0?
cards.solution: -3/4 = -0.75, which lies between 0 and -1, closer to -1.

cards.title: Fountain Regular Pentagon
cards.expectedAnswer:
All five sides=4m
All interior angles=108
acceptableAnswers:
All five sides=4m
All interior angles=108
cards.problemText: Fountain Design: A fountain is a regular pentagon. One of the sides is 4 meters long, and one of the interior angles measures 108°. What are the lengths of the other sides and the measures of the other angles?
cards.solution: In any regular polygon, all sides are congruent (4 m) and all interior angles are congruent (108°).

cards.title: Park Entrance Supplementary Angles
cards.problemText: Park Entrance: Two paths meet at the park entrance and form a pair of supplementary angles. If one angle measures 110°, what is the measure of the other angle?
cards.solution: Supplementary angles sum to 180°: 180° - 110° = 70°.

cards.title: Triangle Angle Sum Theorem
cards.problemText: Jose will draw a triangle using a protractor. Which set of angle measures can form a triangle?
cards.solution: The interior angles of a triangle must sum to exactly 180°: 42° + 58° + 80° = 180°.

cards.title: Classifying Non-Convex Polygons
cards.problemText:
Which classification correctly describes the two polygons shown below?
[IMAGE: Concave Polygons with Reflex Angles]
cards.solution: Polygons with unequal properties are irregular, and an interior angle > 180° makes them non-convex (concave).

cards.title: Intersecting Lines Angle Measures
cards.problemText:
Two straight lines intersect as shown. If one angle measures 76°, which statement is correct?
[IMAGE: Intersecting lines with angles x, y, z, and 76°]
cards.solution: Vertical angle y = 76°. Adjacent supplementary angles x = z = 180° - 76° = 104°.

cards.title: Average Runner Speed
cards.problemText: A runner completes a 200-meter race in 20 seconds. What is the average speed?
cards.solution: Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 200 m ÷ 20 s = 10 m/s.

cards.title: Photocopy Machine Rate
cards.problemText: If a RISO machine can produce 120 photocopy papers in 3 hours, how many papers will be produced in 5 hours?
cards.solution: Rate = 120 ÷ 3 = 40 papers/hr. In 5 hours: 40 × 5 = 200 papers.

cards.title: Speed Comparison
cards.problemText: Car A travels 200 kilometers 5 hours, while Car B travels 240 kilometers in 4 hours. Which vehicle is faster, and what is its speed?
cards.solution: Speed A = 200/5 = 40 km/h. Speed B = 240/4 = 60 km/h. Car B is faster at 60 km/h.

cards.title: Repeating Decimal to Fraction
cards.problemText: What is the equivalent fraction of 0.666…?

cards.title: Mixed Number to Improper Fraction
cards.problemText: What is 8 5/6 expressed as an improper fraction?

cards.title: Rational Numbers on Number Line
cards.problemText:
Which of the following number lines shows the correct plotting of rational numbers -3.0, 0 and 5.5?
[IMAGE: Option A - Number line with points at -3, 0, 5.5]
[IMAGE: Option B - Number line with points at -5.5, -3, 0]
[IMAGE: Option C - Number line with points at 0, 3, 5.5]
[IMAGE: Option D - Number line with points at -5.5, 0, 3]
cards.solution: Negative rational numbers lie to the left of zero, and positive rational numbers lie to the right.

cards.title: Locating 7/4 on Number Line
cards.problemText:
Which of the points below best describes 74 ?
[IMAGE: Number line with labeled points M, A, T, H]
cards.solution: 7/4 = 1.75, which lies between 1 and 2, closer to 2.

cards.title: Ascending Order of Real Numbers
cards.problemText: Arrange the following numbers in ascending order.              6,   72,   5.6
cards.solution: Convert 7/2 to 3.5. Comparing 3.5 < 5.6 < 6 gives: 7/2, 5.6, 6.

cards.title: Electronics Commission Calculation
cards.problemText: Gregorio works at an electronics store where he earns a 5% commission on his sales. Customers who pay in full receive a 10% discount, and a 12% sales tax is added after the discount. Gregorio sold a tablet originally priced at ₱18,000. How much will Gregorio earn from the sale?

cards.title: Discount Calculation
cards.problemText: Gregorio works at an electronics store where he earns a 5% commission on his sales. Customers who pay in full receive a 10% discount, and a 12% sales tax is added after the discount. Gregorio sold a tablet originally priced at ₱18,000. How much is the 10% discount?

cards.title: Running Trail Lap Time
cards.problemText: Running Trail: The park has a 400-meter running trail. A runner moves at a constant speed of 2 meters per second. How many seconds does the runner need to complete one lap (400 meters)?
cards.solution: Time = Distance ÷ Speed = 400 m ÷ 2 m/s = 200 seconds.

cards.title: Park Distance Signs Ordering
cards.problemText: Distance Signs: The park entrance has signs showing the distances to four areas: 0.1 km, 14 km, 0.75 km, and 12 km. Arrange the distances from the nearest to the farthest from the entrance.
cards.solution: Convert all to decimals: 0.1 km, 0.25 km (1/4), 0.50 km (1/2), 0.75 km. Order: 0.1 km, 1/4 km, 1/2 km, 0.75 km.

cards.title: Simplest Form of Rational Expressions
cards.expectedAnswer: When the numerator and denominator have no common factors other than 1.
acceptableAnswers: When the numerator and denominator have no common factors other than 1.
cards.problemText: When is a rational algebraic expression considered to be in its simplest form?
cards.solution: A rational expression is in simplest form when numerator and denominator have no common factors other than ±1.

cards.title: Multiplying Rational Expressions First Step
cards.expectedAnswer: Factor all numerators and denominators completely.
acceptableAnswers: Factor all numerators and denominators completely.
cards.problemText: What is the first step before multiplying rational algebraic expressions containing polynomials x2-9x+2⋅x+2x+3 ?
cards.solution: Factoring all numerators and denominators completely allows you to simplify common factors before multiplying.

cards.title: Product of Monomial Fractions
cards.problemText: What is the product of the expression 2x⋅3y?
cards.solution: Multiply numerators and denominators: (2 * 3) / (x * y) = 6 / (xy).

cards.title: Reciprocal of Rational Expression
cards.problemText: What is the reciprocal (multiplicative inverse) of the rational expression x-3x+5 ?
cards.solution: The reciprocal of A/B is B/A: the reciprocal of (x - 3)/(x + 5) is (x + 5)/(x - 3).

cards.title: Division Process for Rational Expressions
cards.problemText: Which of the following describes the correct process for dividing two rational algebraic expressions, AB÷CD?
cards.solution: Dividing by a fraction is equivalent to multiplying by its reciprocal: (A/B) ÷ (C/D) = (A/B) * (D/C).

cards.title: GCF of Polynomial
cards.problemText: To factor the polynomial 8x2-12x, the greatest common factor (GCF) of the terms is ______.
cards.solution: GCF of coefficients 8 and 12 is 4, and common variable factor is x: GCF = 4x.

cards.title: Difference of Two Squares Factors
cards.problemText: The factors of the difference of two squares are always a pair of __________.
cards.solution: a² - b² factors into conjugate binomials: (a - b)(a + b).

cards.title: Perfect Square Trinomial Factoring
cards.problemText: A perfect square trinomial always factors into the ______ of a binomial.
cards.solution: a² + 2ab + b² = (a + b)², which is the square of a binomial.

cards.title: Product of Sum and Difference
cards.expectedAnswer: b, the coefficient of the middle term
acceptableAnswers: b, the coefficient of the middle term
cards.problemText: To factor general trinomial x2+bx+c, find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is ___________.

cards.title: Square of Binomial Expansion
cards.problemText: Before cancelling common factors in a rational algebraic expression, you must first  _______ both the numerator and denominator completely.

cards.title: Factoring Simple Trinomials
cards.problemText: Is the statement true or false: When multiplying simple monomials with the same base, you subtract their exponents.
cards.solution: Find numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5: 2 and 3 => (x + 2)(x + 3).

cards.title: Factoring Difference of Squares
cards.problemText: Make the statement true: To multiply rational algebraic expressions, you multiply the numerators together and multiply the (numerators/denominators) together.

cards.title: Simplifying Rational Expressions
cards.problemText:
Replace the underlined phrase to make the statement right:
The operation ab÷cd is equivalent to ab divided by dc.
cards.solution: Factor numerator: 3(x + 2) / 3 = x + 2.

cards.title: Property in Multiplying Polynomials
cards.problemText: What property will you use in multiplying 3x (2x+5)?
cards.solution: The Distributive Property a(b + c) = ab + ac distributes 3x to both 2x and 5.

cards.title: Identifying Non-Special Products
cards.problemText: Which of the following expression pairs is NOT an example of a special product?
cards.solution: (x + 4)(x - 3) gives a general trinomial x² + x - 12, unlike differences of squares or perfect squares.

cards.title: Area of Square with Binomial Side
cards.expectedAnswer: The middle term must always be positive.
acceptableAnswers: The middle term must always be positive.
cards.problemText: Which condition is NOT required for a trinomial ax2+bx+c to be a Perfect Square Trinomial?

answers.text: The first and last terms must be perfect squares.
The middle term must be twice the product of square roots of the first and last terms.
The last term must always be positive.
The middle term must always be positive.

cards.title: Multiplying Reciprocal Fractions
cards.problemText: Maria factored the polynomial x2+7x+12. What pair of numbers should she need to consider?
cards.solution: All terms in numerator and denominator cancel: ((x - 2)(x + 3)) / ((x + 3)(x - 2)) = 1.

cards.title: Dividing Monomial Algebraic Fractions
cards.problemText: What expression is equivalent to 12x4?

cards.title: Completing Perfect Square Trinomial
cards.problemText: Write an expression equivalent to x5÷2y?
cards.solution: Take half the middle coefficient squared: (8 / 2)² = 4² = 16.

cards.title: Complete Factoring of Trinomial
cards.problemText: Is the statement true or false: The product of (x-4)(x+4) is equal to x2-16 because the product of the sum and difference of two terms always results in a difference of two squares.
cards.solution: Factor out GCF 2: 2(x² + 5x + 6) = 2(x + 2)(x + 3).

cards.title: Simplifying Rational Fraction with Difference of Squares
cards.problemText: Find the error in the given statement: Finding the dimensions of a rectangular garden given its area expression x2-2x-15 requires finding two factors whose sum is 2 and whose product is -15.
cards.solution: Factor numerator as (x - 4)(x + 4). Cancel (x - 4): result is x + 4.

cards.title: Expanding Monomial by Binomial
cards.problemText: What is the product of 3x (2x+5)?
cards.solution: Distribute 3x: 3x(2x) + 3x(5) = 6x² + 15x.

cards.title: Rectangular Board Area Claim
cards.expectedAnswer: No, the correct area is x2-49.
acceptableAnswers: No, the correct area is x2-49.
cards.problemText: A rectangular bulletin board has a length of (x+7) m and a width of (x-7) m. A student claims the area is x2+49m2. Is the student correct? Why?
cards.solution: Area = (x + 7)(x - 7) = x² - 49 (difference of two squares). The student's sign was incorrect.

cards.title: Multiplying Complex Rational Expressions
cards.problemText: The side of a square stage is increased by 2 meters. If the original side length is x meters, what expression represents the new area of the stage?
cards.solution: Factor x² - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3). Cancel common factors (x + 2) and (x + 3) to get x - 3.

cards.title: Dividing Complex Rational Expressions
cards.problemText: Each student uses 3x5 meter of string for a Science project. If 10 students join the activity, what is the total length of string needed?
cards.solution: Multiply by reciprocal: ((x - 2)(x + 2) / (x + 1)) * ((x + 1) / (x - 2)) = x + 2.

cards.title: Factoring Binomial Difference
cards.expectedAnswer: Yes, the solution is completely correct.
acceptableAnswers: Yes, the solution is completely correct.
cards.problemText:
Did the student evaluate and simplify this expression correctly?
Multiply: 3x⋅x6       Step 1: 3⋅xx⋅6
Step 2: 36=12
cards.solution: Factor out 3: 3(x² - 9) = 3(x - 3)(x + 3).

cards.title: FOIL Binomial Product
cards.problemText: What is the factored form of 9x2-25?

cards.title: Rational Expression Simplification
cards.problemText: The factored form of x2+6x+9 is ______.

cards.title: Garden Area Modification
cards.problemText: What are the factors of x2+7x+12?
cards.solution: Original = x²; New = (x + 3)(x - 3) = x² - 9. The new area is 9 m² less.

cards.title: Adding Fractions with Like Denominators
cards.problemText: What is the simplest form of x29x+3 ?
cards.solution: Combine numerators over the common denominator: (2 + 3) / (x - 1) = 5 / (x - 1).

cards.title: Finding Dimensions from Area
cards.problemText: You are designing a square picture frame. The outer edge of the frame is a square with side length x cm. The inner opening (where the photo goes) is a square with side length y cm. Write the expression for the surface area of the border (the frame around the photo).
cards.solution: Factor x² + 9x + 20 into (x + 4)(x + 5).

cards.title: Undefined Rational Expression Value
cards.problemText:
An architecture student is finding the side length of a square room with a floor area given by: Area=25x2-30x+9.
The student claims the room’s side length is 5x+3 meters because 25x2=5x and 9=3. Did the student use the correct sign in their binomial factor (5x+3)? If not, why?
cards.solution: Set denominator to zero: x - 7 = 0 => x = 7.

cards.title: Factoring by Grouping
cards.problemText:
Two students, Leo and Maya, were asked to factor the simple trinomial x2-2x-24. Their final answers are shown below:
Leo's Answer: (x-6)(x+4)
Maya's Answer: (x+6)(x-4)
Which student has the correct factored form?

cards.title: Finding Slope from Equation
cards.problemText: What is the slope of the line represented by the equation y=3x-5?
cards.solution: In slope-intercept form y = mx + b, slope m = 3.

cards.title: Finding Y-Intercept Ordered Pair
cards.problemText: What ordered pair represents the y-intercept of the line y=2x+7?
cards.solution: At x = 0, y = 2(0) + 7 = 7, giving the ordered pair (0, 7).

cards.title: Slope of Horizontal Line
cards.problemText:
In parallelogram KLMN, if KL=12cm, what is the length of NM?
[IMAGE: Parallelogram KLMN]
cards.solution: Horizontal lines have a vertical change (rise) of 0, so slope m = 0.

cards.title: Slope of Vertical Line
cards.problemText: If m∠KLM=70°, what is the measure of its adjacent angle?
cards.solution: Vertical lines have a horizontal change (run) of 0; dividing by 0 makes the slope undefined.

cards.title: Slope-Intercept Form Form
cards.problemText: Opposite angles of a parallelogram are ______________.
cards.solution: y = mx + b is the standard slope-intercept form.

cards.title: Definition of Parallelogram
cards.problemText: If the perimeter of a parallelogram is 36 cm and one pair of side is 10cm, what is the length of the other side?
cards.solution: A parallelogram is defined by having two pairs of parallel opposite sides.

cards.title: Consecutive Angles in Parallelogram
cards.problemText: If the diagonals of parallelogram ABCD intersect at E and AE=8cm, what is AC?
cards.solution: Consecutive angles lie between parallel lines and are supplementary (sum = 180°).

cards.title: Opposite Angles in Parallelogram
cards.problemText: This refers to a quadrilateral with four right angles and four equal sides.
cards.solution: Opposite angles in every parallelogram are congruent (equal in measure).

cards.title: Equiangular Parallelogram
cards.problemText: The graph of y=-2x+4 crosses the y-axis at (0,4), what does the point (0,4) represent?
cards.solution: An equiangular parallelogram has four 90° angles and is called a rectangle.

cards.title: Equilateral Parallelogram
cards.problemText: What condition guarantees that two lines are parallel?
cards.solution: An equilateral parallelogram is called a rhombus.

cards.title: Y-Intercept of Line
cards.problemText: In parallelogram ABCD, AB∥CD. If ∠A=65°, what is ∠C?
cards.solution: At x = 0, y = -9, so the y-intercept is (0, -9).

cards.title: Slope through Origin
cards.problemText: Name one pair of consecutive angles in parallelogram ABCD.

cards.title: Quadrilateral Interior Angles Sum
cards.problemText: In a square, all angles measure______.

cards.title: Y-Intercept of Proportional Line
cards.problemText:
A rectangle has dimensions of 15 cm in length and 8 cm in width, which equation represents its perimeter?
2(15)(8) or 215+2(8)
cards.solution: y = 5x + 0, so the line passes through the origin (0, 0).

cards.title: Bisecting Diagonals Quadrilateral
cards.problemText: If the diagonals of a quadrilateral bisect each other, what type of a quadrilateral must it be?
cards.solution: A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other is a parallelogram.

cards.title: Slope Between Two Points
cards.problemText: A line passes through (2,3) and (6,11). What is its slope?

cards.title: Evaluating Linear Function
cards.problemText: In the linear function fx=2x-6, what is f(5)?

cards.title: Tricycle Fare Model
cards.problemText: A tricycle charges a ₱20 starting fare plus ₱5 for every additional kilometer. What is the equation that represents the total fare F for x additional kilometers?
cards.solution: Base fare = ₱20, rate = ₱5/km => Total Fare F = 5x + 20.

cards.title: Perpendicular Slope Calculation
cards.problemText: A line has slope 2. What must be the slope of the line perpendicular to it?
cards.solution: Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes: m_perp = -1 / 2.

cards.title: Line Equation from Slope & Intercept
cards.problemText: A line passes through (0,3) and has slope -2. What equation represents the line?
cards.solution: Using y = mx + b with m = -2 and b = 3: y = -2x + 3.

cards.title: Congruent Diagonals Parallelogram
cards.problemText: What kind of a parallelogram has congruent diagonals?
cards.solution: A parallelogram has equal-length diagonals if and only if it is a rectangle.

cards.title: Opposite Side Length in Parallelogram
cards.problemText: In parallelogram ABCD, AB=14cm. What is CD?
cards.solution: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent: CD = AB = 14 cm.

cards.title: Rectangle Area Calculation
cards.problemText: What is the area of a rectangle which sides are 5cm and 7cm?
cards.solution: Area = length × width = 5 cm × 7 cm = 35 cm².

cards.title: Parallel Lines Slope Value
cards.problemText: Two lines have slopes 4 and m. If they are parallel, what is m?
cards.solution: Parallel lines have identical slopes, so m = 4.

cards.title: Slope Identification
cards.problemText: In the equation y=3x-2, what is the slope?
cards.solution: In y = mx + b, slope m is the coefficient of x: m = 3.

cards.title: Interpreting Linear Constant
cards.problemText: A taxi fare is modeled by F=10d+50, where d is the number of kilometers traveled. What does the number 50 represent?
cards.solution: When distance d = 0, F = 50. The constant represents the initial fixed base fare.

cards.title: Identifying Perpendicular Slopes
cards.problemText: Two lines have slope 4 and -14 . What relationship do the two lines have?
cards.solution: Product of slopes = 4 × (-1/4) = -1, which defines perpendicular lines.

cards.title: Lines with Equal Slopes
cards.problemText: Two lines have the same slopes equal to 2. What relationship do the two lines have?
cards.solution: Lines with equal slopes in the same plane are parallel.

cards.title: Square Flower Bed Area
cards.problemText: A rectangular school garden measures 18m by 10m. A square flower bed with side lengths of 6m is placed inside the garden. What is the area of the flower bed?
cards.solution: Area of square = side² = 6 m × 6 m = 36 m².

cards.title: Parallelogram Proof Property
cards.expectedAnswer: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if both pairs of opposite sides are congruent.
acceptableAnswers: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if both pairs of opposite sides are congruent.
cards.problemText:
Quadrilateral ABCD has the following side lengths. What property shows that it is a parallelogram?
[IMAGE: Rectangle ABCD with sides AB=12cm, CD=12cm, AD=8cm, BC=8cm]
cards.solution: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram if and only if both pairs of opposite sides are congruent.

cards.title: Parallel Slopes Reasoning
cards.problemText:
Students claim that:
Student A: Two lines are parallel because they both have a slope of 3.
Student B: Two lines are perpendicular because they both have a slope of 3.
Which student is correct?
cards.solution: Equal slopes mean parallel lines, so Student A is correct.

cards.title: Fence Perimeter Calculation
cards.problemText: A rectangular fence has measurements of 10m and 8m on the sides. What is its perimeter?
cards.solution: Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(10 + 8) = 2(18) = 36 m.

cards.title: Vegetable Garden Dimensions
cards.problemText: The Grade 9 students want to create a rectangular vegetable garden with an area of exactly 120m2. The garden must have a length greater than its width. Give two possible dimensions of the garden.
cards.solution: Possible factor pairs where Length > Width: 15m × 8m, 12m × 10m, 20m × 6m, 24m × 5m, 30m × 4m, 40m × 3m, 60m × 2m, 120m × 1m.

cards.title: Bridge Boundary Slopes
cards.expectedAnswer: The slopes of boundaries A and B are both 2.
acceptableAnswers: The slopes of boundaries A and B are both 2.
cards.problemText:
CSNHS is improving its walkway system to make it easier to move between buildings. They constructed rectangular bridges between buildings. Two bridge boundaries are represented by the lines:
Boundary A: y=2x+3
Boundary B: y-2x=10
What is the slope of Boundary A and Boundary B?
cards.solution: Boundary A has m = 2. Boundary B is y = 2x + 10, which also has m = 2.

cards.title: Picnic Platform Flooring Area
cards.problemText: A local community is preparing a picnic area in a public park. The main picnic platform is designed in the shape of a rectangle measuring 15m and 10m wide. Inside the platform is decorative stone area designed as a square. Each side of the square measures 6m. The organizer wants to cover the area outside the square with an outdoor flooring. What is its area?
cards.solution: Platform area = 15 × 10 = 150 m². Square stone area = 6 × 6 = 36 m². Flooring area = 150 - 36 = 114 m².

cards.title: Border Material Sufficiency
cards.expectedAnswer: Yes, because the perimeter of the square is only 24m.
acceptableAnswers: Yes, because the perimeter of the square is only 24m.
cards.problemText: A local community is preparing a picnic area in a public park. The main picnic platform is designed in the shape of a rectangle measuring 15m and 10m wide. Inside the platform is decorative stone area designed as a square. Each side of the square measures 6m. The organizers will place the border around the square-shape stone area. They have 25 meters of border material. Is this enough? Why?
cards.solution: Perimeter of the square = 4 × 6 m = 24 m. Since 25 m > 24 m, the material is enough.

cards.title: DMS to Decimal Degrees
cards.problemText: Convert the angle measure 450330' into decimal degree.

cards.title: Decimal Degrees to DMS
cards.problemText: Which of the following degree, minute, and seconds is equal to the angle measure 12.080?

cards.title: Mt. Isarog Field Triangle Classification
cards.problemText: A triangular field near Mt. Isarog has sides 30m, 40m, and 50m. What type of triangle is it?
cards.solution: 30² + 40² = 900 + 1600 = 2500 = 50². By Pythagorean Theorem, it is a right triangle.

cards.title: Obtuse Triangle Classification
cards.problemText: The largest angle of an oblique triangle measures 1100, the triangle is classified as:
cards.solution: Any triangle with an interior angle greater than 90° is an obtuse triangle.

cards.title: Acute Triangle Classification
cards.problemText: If all three angles of a triangle are less than 900, the triangle is ____.
cards.solution: A triangle in which all three angles measure less than 90° is an acute triangle.

cards.title: Types of Oblique Triangles
cards.problemText: An oblique triangle can be classified according to its angles as ____.
cards.solution: Non-right (oblique) triangles are either acute (all angles < 90°) or obtuse (one angle > 90°).

cards.title: Law of Sines Equation
cards.problemText: What formula represents the Law of Sines?
cards.solution: The Law of Sines states: a / sin(A) = b / sin(B) = c / sin(C).

cards.title: Law of Cosines Equation
cards.problemText: What formula represents the Law of Cosines?
cards.solution: The Law of Cosines is a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos(A).

cards.title: Triangular Garden in Naga City
cards.problemText: A triangular garden in Naga City has two sides measuring 12m and 15m with an included angle of 700. Which law should be used to find the third side?
cards.solution: When given two sides and the included angle (SAS), the Law of Cosines is used.

cards.title: Included Angle Identification
cards.solution: The angle formed between sides AC and BC sharing vertex C is ∠C.

cards.title: Naga City Rescue Route Measurement
cards.problemText: A rescue team in Naga City needs to determine the distance between two locations that cannot be directly measured. The team knows two sides of a triangular route and the angle between them. Which method is most appropriate, Law of Sines or Law of Cosines?
cards.solution: Given two sides and the included angle (SAS), the Law of Cosines is appropriate.

cards.title: Flagpole Height Elevation
cards.problemText: An observer stands exactly 15 meters away from the base of a vertical flagpole. The angle of elevation from the observer’s feet to the top of the flagpole is 450. How tall is the flagpole?
cards.solution: tan(45°) = height / distance => 1 = h / 15 => h = 15 meters.

cards.title: Third Angle in Triangle
cards.problemText: In ∆ABC, ∠A=450 and ∠C=600. What is the measure of ∠B?
cards.solution: Sum of angles in a triangle is 180°: ∠B = 180° - 45° - 60° = 75°.

cards.title: Catanduanes Fisherman Law of Sines
cards.expectedAnswer: At least one known side and its opposite angle.
acceptableAnswers: At least one known side and its opposite angle.
cards.problemText: A fisherman in the waters near Catanduanes observes two landmarks that are 20km apart. The angles formed by the two landmarks and the fishing boat are 450 and 650. What information is needed to solve for an unknown side using the Law of Sines.
cards.solution: The Law of Sines requires at least one side and its corresponding opposite angle pair.

cards.title: Law of Sines Side Length
cards.problemText: In ∆ABC, ∠A=250, ∠B=850, and AC=10cm. What is the approximate length of BC? Formula: BC=10sin25sin85

cards.title: Pasacao Boat Navigation Angle
cards.problemText: A boat travels from Pasacao toward a point offshore. The distance between two observation points is 25km. If the observed angles are 400 and 700, what is the third angle of the triangle?

cards.title: Law of Cosines Formulation
cards.problemText: In ∆DEF, side d=10cm, side f=12cm and ∠E=600. Which equation correctly determines side e?
cards.solution: By Law of Cosines for side e opposite ∠E: e² = d² + f² - 2df cos(E) = 10² + 12² - 2(10)(12)cos(60°).

cards.title: Triangle Angle via Law of Sines
cards.problemText: Determine the measure of ∠C in ∆ABC if AB=0.77km, m∠A=1100, and BC=1.25 km.

cards.title: Triangular Lot Third Side
cards.problemText: A triangular lot has sides 10m and 14m with an included angle of 600. What is the approximate length of the third side?

cards.title: Surveyor Triangular Area Third Side
cards.problemText: A surveyor measures two sides of a triangular area as 20m and 30m and the included angle as 450. What is the approximate third side?

cards.title: Angle Measure from Law of Cosines
cards.problemText: What is m∠E in the equation 102=82+122-2812cosE?

cards.title: Law of Sines Side Computation
cards.problemText: In ∆ABC, ∠A=450, ∠B=750, and side a=10cm. Using the law of sines, approximately how long is side b?

cards.title: Triangle PQR Side Length
cards.problemText: In ∆PQR, ∠P=300, ∠Q=520, and side r=12 cm. What is the approximate length of side p?

cards.title: The Water Tank Portal
cards.problemText: The water tank is 35 full. After 24 liters of water are added, the tank becomes 34 full. What is the total capacity of the tank?
cards.solution: The added water is 3/4 - 3/5 = 3/20 of the tank. Since 3/20 of the capacity is 24 liters, the capacity is 24 × 20 ÷ 3 = 160 liters.

cards.title: Pedro's Two-Day Journey
cards.problemText: Pedro traveled for two consecutive days. On day 1, he drove his van at an average speed of 50 km/hr for 4 hours. On day 2, he drove at an average speed of 60 km/hr for 3 hours. What is the total distance, in kilometers, that Pedro drove over the two days?

cards.title: Consecutive Odd Integers
cards.problemText: The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 147. What are the smallest and largest integers?
cards.solution: Let the integers be n - 2, n, and n + 2. Then 3n = 147, so n = 49. The integers are 47, 49, and 51.

cards.title: The Rectangle Portal
cards.problemText: A rectangle has a perimeter of 64cm. Its length is 8cm more than twice its width. Find the area of the rectangle.
cards.solution: The supplied challenge gives length 20 cm and width 12 cm. Therefore, the area is 20 × 12 = 240 cm².

cards.title: Across the River
cards.problemText:
A surveyor wants to determine the distance between two points, A and B, located on opposite sides of a river. From a point C on the same side of the river as A, the surveyor measures CA = 80 m, CB = 120 m, and ∠ACB=65° .
Using the law of cosines, what is the distance from point A to point B?
cards.solution: AB² = 80² + 120² - 2(80)(120)cos(65°), which gives AB ≈ 112.7 meters.

cards.title: Simple Interest Relationship
cards.expectedAnswer:
I=Prt
Where,I = simple interest
P= principal amount
r= annual interest rate
t = time in years
acceptableAnswers:
I=Prt
Where,I = simple interest
P= principal amount
r= annual interest rate
t = time in years
cards.problemText: Ana invested ₱8,000 in a savings account that earns simple interest at a rate of 5% per year. The interest is earned based on the original amount invested, the interest rate, and the length of time the money remains invested. What mathematical equation correctly represents the relationship used to find the simple interest (I)?
cards.solution: Simple interest is I = Prt, where P is principal, r is the annual rate, and t is time in years.

cards.title: Discount at the Market
cards.problemText: Liza buys a bag with a marked price of ₱1,200 at a 15% discount. How much discount does she get?

cards.title: Sales Tax
cards.problemText: Marco bought a desk lamp priced at ₱850.00. If the store charges a 12% sales tax, how much is the sales tax on the item?

cards.title: Weekly Food Budget
cards.problemText: Juan earns ₱500 a week in allowance. He plans to save 20% for emergency funds, spend 50% on food, and save the rest for a school project. How much will he spend on food each week?

cards.title: Simplest Form
cards.expectedAnswer: The GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1.
acceptableAnswers: The GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1.
cards.problemText: What does it mean when a fraction is in simplest form?

answers.text: The numerator is always smaller than the denominator.
The GCF of the numerator and denominator is 1.

cards.solution: A fraction is in simplest form when its numerator and denominator have no common factor other than 1.

cards.title: Multiplicative Inverse
cards.problemText: The expression x+4x-7 is an example of rational expression. What is its multiplicative inverse?
cards.solution: The multiplicative inverse interchanges the numerator and denominator.

cards.title: Expanded Garden Area
cards.problemText: The side of a square garden is increased by 3 meters. If the original side length is x meters, what expression represents the new area of the garden?
cards.solution: The new side is x + 3, so (x + 3)² = x² + 6x + 9.

cards.title: String for Twelve
cards.problemText: If one student uses x meters of string for a Science project, how much string will be needed for 12 students? Express your answer algebraically.
cards.solution: Twelve students use 12 × x = 12x meters.

cards.title: Finding the GCF
cards.problemText: Two students simplified the expression 12x3y-18x2y2+24xy3. Student says the GCF is 6xy while student B says the GCF is 6xy(x-y+2y). Who is correct?
cards.solution: The numerical GCF is 6 and the common variables are x and y, so the GCF is 6xy.

cards.title: Simplifying a Rational Expression
cards.problemText: A student said that the simplified form of the rational expression x2-9x2+5x+6 is x-3x+2. Is the student correct?
cards.solution: Factoring gives (x - 3)(x + 3) / [(x + 2)(x + 3)] = (x - 3)/(x + 2).

cards.title: Perpendicular Lines
cards.problemText: What is the relationship between two lines that intersect to form a 90-degree angle?
cards.solution: Lines that intersect at a right angle are perpendicular.

cards.title: Square and Rectangle
cards.expectedAnswer: Because square have four right angles like a rectangle
acceptableAnswers: Because square have four right angles like a rectangle
cards.problemText: Why is every square considered a rectangle?
cards.solution: A rectangle is a quadrilateral with four right angles. A square meets that definition.

cards.title: Parallelogram Side Equality
cards.problemText: If ABCD is a parallelogram and AB=3x+5 and CD=x+15, what does this imply about the value of x?
cards.solution: Opposite sides are equal: 3x + 5 = x + 15, so x = 5.

cards.title: Unknown Figure Value
cards.problemText:
What is the value of x in the given figure?
[IMAGE: Parallel lines cut by a transversal with angles 60° and 8x - 4]
cards.solution: Using the equal-side or angle relationship shown in the supplied figure gives x = 8.

cards.title: Choosing a Square Court
cards.problemText: Which court is designed in the shape of a square?
cards.solution: A square has four equal sides and four right angles, matching Court A.

cards.title: SAS Triangle Law
cards.problemText: Which trigonometric law should be used first when given two sides and the included angle (SAS) of an oblique triangle?
cards.solution: The Law of Cosines directly relates two sides and their included angle to the third side.

cards.title: Included Angle
cards.problemText:
The included angle of sides AC and BC in ∆ABC is
[IMAGE: Triangle ABC]
cards.solution: Sides AC and BC share endpoint C, so their included angle is ∠C.

cards.title: Angle BCD
cards.problemText:
Given the figure, what is the measure of ∠BCD?
[IMAGE: Triangle ABD with segment BC, showing angles and side lengths]
cards.solution: Applying the angle relationships shown in the supplied figure gives 103°.

cards.title: Law of Cosines Formula
cards.problemText:
In △DEF, side d = 8 cm, side f = 11 cm, and angle E = 60°. Which formula correctly calculates the length of side e?
[IMAGE: Figure 3 showing △DEF with side d=8cm, f=11cm, ∠D=60°]
cards.solution: Side e is opposite the included angle E, so the Law of Cosines uses subtraction.

cards.title: Triangle Angle Sum
cards.problemText:
In △PQR, angle P = 30°, angle Q = 45°, and side r = 12 cm. What is the measure of angle R?
[IMAGE: Figure 2 showing △PQR with ∠P=30°, ∠Q=45°, r=12cm]
cards.solution: The angles of a triangle total 180°, so R = 180° - 30° - 45° = 105°.
